syllable_structure: Thai syllable phonotactics and structure rules

components.C1: Initial consonant (optional in some cases, mandatory in most)

live_syllable.definition: Syllable ending with long vowel OR sonorant final
conditions: Sonorant final (ง น ม ย ว ร ล)

dead_syllable.definition: Syllable ending with short vowel + stop OR short vowel alone
conditions: Short vowel + stop final (ก จ ด ต บ ป)
Short vowel with no final (rare, only with ะ)
dead_syllable.note: Short vowel + sonorant is LIVE, not dead

consonant_clusters.description: Valid C1+C2 clusters in initial position

fricative_liquid.note: ทร is pronounced /s/ in modern Thai, not /tʰr/

cluster_tone_rule.description: Cluster tone class determined by C1
cluster_tone_rule.rule: C1 determines consonant class for tone calculation

invalid_clusters.description: Clusters that do not occur in Thai
invalid_clusters.note: If these appear, syllable boundary is between them

leading_h_modification.description: ห leading before low-class sonorant changes effective class to high
leading_h_modification.pattern: ห + [ง น ม ย ร ล ว]
leading_h_modification.rule: ห is silent, but makes following consonant behave as high class for tone

leading_o_modification.description: อ leading before consonant makes it behave as mid class
leading_o_modification.rule: อ is silent, but changes effective class to mid for tone
leading_o_modification.note: Less common than ห leading, used in specific words

implicit_vowel.description: Consonant without written vowel has inherent vowel
implicit_vowel.exceptions: Does not apply when consonant is clearly final or in cluster

syllable_boundary_rules.description: Rules for dividing words into syllables
rules: CVC.CV - final consonant belongs to first syllable if valid
Invalid cluster → syllable boundary between consonants
